original_content.worked_solution:
The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{3}=1,{a}_{2}=0,{a}_{1}=2,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right){\sin }^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({\sin }^{2}⁡x)+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sin }^{2}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+2\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡2x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\end{aligned}
$$

corrected_content.worked_solution:
The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{3}=1,{a}_{2}=0,{a}_{1}=2,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({\sin}^{2}x) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right){\sin }^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({\sin }^{2}⁡x)+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sin }^{2}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+2\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡2x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\end{aligned}
$$

rationale: The given input is sin^2(x), so the first application must be D(sin^2(x)), not D(cos(2x)). Subsequent source derivatives and final answer -2sin(2x) already apply to sin^2(x); correcting the copied argument makes the entire chain consistent.
